user.title: Sign in to Wattnet
user.description:
Wattnet provides the carbon footprint, water footprint and environmental score of the electricity consumed in each European zone.

Sign in with a Wattnet credential: its client ID and client secret. You can get one by creating a free account at [developers.wattnet.eu]({developer_portal_url}).

data_description.client_id: The client ID of your Wattnet credential.
data_description.client_secret: Stored in Home Assistant so the integration can request a fresh access token whenever the previous one expires.

zone.title: Choose your zone
zone.description: Pick the electricity zone to monitor. Your home location is preselected when it falls inside a Wattnet zone. You can add the integration again for more zones.

data_description.zone: Electricity bidding zone, labelled with its full name and code.
data_description.scope: Life cycle also counts the impact of building, fuelling and maintaining the power plants. Operational only counts the electricity generation itself.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Wattnet again
reauth_confirm.description: Wattnet rejected the stored credentials, for example because the credential was regenerated or deleted. Enter the client ID and client secret of your Wattnet credential again.

data_description.client_id: The client ID of your Wattnet credential.
data_description.client_secret: The current client secret of your Wattnet credential.

reconfigure.title: Change zone
reconfigure.description: Choose the zone to monitor. Statistics already imported for the previous zone are kept in Home Assistant.

data_description.zone: Electricity bidding zone, labelled with its full name and code.

error.invalid_auth: Wattnet did not accept this client ID and client secret. Check them, and that the credential is active.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Wattnet. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.reauth_successful: Signed in again. The integration is working.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Zone changed. The integration was reloaded.
abort.invalid_auth: Wattnet did not accept the stored credentials. Use the re-authentication option first.

data_description.scope: Life cycle also counts building, fuelling and maintaining the power plants; operational only the generation. Changing it starts a new set of statistics.
data_description.update_interval: Updates run at fixed times, on each quarter hour, when Wattnet publishes a data point (every 15 minutes), and ask again for a few minutes if it is not out yet. Provisional data is re-imported on every update until Wattnet consolidates it.
data_description.backfill_days: Days of history imported the first time a metric is fetched. Use the Re-import statistics action to load more later.
data_description.show_dashboard: Adds the Wattnet dashboard to the sidebar, with the footprint of each zone set up in this installation. It uses the Wattnet logo and disappears when the last zone that asks for it is removed.

reimport_statistics.name: Re-import statistics
reimport_statistics.description: Forgets what was imported and downloads the last days of data again, replacing the statistics. Useful after a gap, or to load more history than the initial import.

config_entry.name: Zone
config_entry.description: The Wattnet zone to re-import. Every zone when left empty.

days.name: Days
days.description: How many days of history to import, from 1 to 90. Defaults to the initial history option.

no_loaded_entry.message: No loaded Wattnet zone matches. Check that the integration is set up and not disabled.

api_unreachable.title: Wattnet is not responding
api_unreachable.description: Wattnet has not answered for more than an hour, so the data for {zone} is unavailable. Home Assistant keeps retrying and will recover on its own. If it persists, check your internet connection and the Wattnet status page.
